result.process_description:
Title: Luxury Airplane

You produce airplanes.
While the base model is always the same, your customer likes to pimp their airplane with fancy interior.
You let them decide between a number of 5 different bars, the number of seats, their color, and the amount of water in the toilets of their plane (you can come up with additional stuff).
After you received the specifications you send the requirements to different teams to manufacture the parts.
E.g. manufacturing the vodka bar is done by the Russian team, the whiskey bar is manufactured by an Irish team.
After receiving the individual bits and pieces, the interior of the plane is assembled, and the plane is sent on a test flight.
During the flight you create a test protocol which is sent to you and the customer.
The plane is delivered to the customer, which has to confirm.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Direct each message flow from sender to receiver. Its endpoints must belong to different pools and be valid interaction nodes.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.

result.rule: When the description states one send action toward a generic set of recipients in one sentence, and a later sentence names several distinct recipient groups, each receiving that same action: Model one send task per named recipient group, each labeled with the send action and that group's name as the description gives it, placed in the order the description gives. Do not replace the named groups with one generic collective task whose label hides them.

When The description states that the process sends a request for a named piece of information to an outside party, and it names the requested information with its own noun phrase.: Model the sending step as a task labeled 'request' followed by the noun phrase the description uses for the requested information. Leave the send action, the recipient and any timing from the description out of the label, and do not replace the requested information's noun phrase with a generic word.

When the description states that the organization's work on an order can start only after the customer has communicated the requirements, and that the organization then starts several activities in parallel: Model the organization's own step of establishing or recording the customer's requirements as a separate task performed by the organization, placed before the parallel split that starts the parallel activities. Do not omit this task just because the description mentions only the customer's communication and the parallel activities.

When the description says the customer selects one value for each configurable attribute of the product, and the value chosen determines which of several downstream partner parties receives a request for that part; the alternatives are described as an either/or selection: Model the selection as an exclusive split gateway with one outgoing sequence flow per possible value. Each flow leads to its own send task addressed to the party responsible for that value. Join the alternative send paths with an exclusive merge gateway before the next common step. Do not route the request for all values through one generic send task, and do not use a parallel gateway for these alternatives.
